summary: Admit explicitly trusted published provenance for legacy redirects introduced after the unchanged audit base

delivery.outcome: An explicit independently configured secondary provenance revision may prove an already published legacy URL existed after the full audit base, while default redirect validation stays strict.
nonGoals: No default relaxation of legacy path provenance.
No audit base reduction, managed-consumer edit, history rewrite, hardware operation, self approval or merge bypass.
Consumer rollout and pin update require independently published upstream source.

architecture.decision: Keep --base as complete audit range. Add a separately trusted immutable redirect provenance input; verify commit type, base ancestry, candidate ancestry and old-path existence without redirect chaining. It must come from protected caller configuration, never untrusted document metadata or inferred checkout origin refs. Final design requires independent policy review.
interfaceChanges: One optional explicit trusted provenance revision input; existing callers retain fail-closed behavior.
architecture.rollback: Revert upstream material commit and leave consumers pinned to their existing published standard.

validation.evidence: All existing tests and negative canaries: new/unproven path, malformed revision, unrelated/later provenance, untracked or unsafe target, redirect chain, missing index and version downgrade remain rejected.
